title: Servepath timing board: percentiles & stream/block decomposition with error overlays
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Goal: Build a Servepath Timing Board that surfaces p50/p95/p99 timings broken down by model and public route, with a clear split between stream vs block (non-stream) IO modes and an overlay for error rates. This ticket coordinates telemetry changes, metric aggregation, dashboard panels and trace linking so product owners and SREs can quickly find regressions and triage cold-start or KV/batching issues.

Background: Current consoles show coarse endpoint latency but do not: 1) separate continuous-stream responses from blocking responses, 2) show percentile trends per model+route, or 3) correlate timing spikes with error classes or batching behavior. This makes it hard to identify whether a tail spike is due to model performance, batching jitter, KV cache misses, or network stalls.

Scope:
- Instrumentation: add span annotations and tags for io_mode ("stream" | "block"), batch_size, kv_cache_hit (true/false) and request_shape (token_count category).
- Metrics pipeline: emit per-request timing to metrics pipeline with labels {model, route, io_mode, tenant, env}. Compute p50/p95/p99 in the TSDB or pre-aggregate in the metrics pipeline depending on cardinality cost.
- Dashboard: implement a multi-row board in Redwood Console with: model/route selector, percentile timeseries (p50/p95/p99), stacked breakdown of io_mode, error-rate overlay (5xx, timeout), request-shape filter, and trace-links on point click.
- Alerts & SLOs: add a canary SLO for tail latency for top 20 routes and a regression alert that triggers when p95 increases by >25% over baseline for 10 minutes.

Success criteria listed below. Implementation should prioritize low-cardinality aggregation and provide fallbacks (sampled traces) to avoid explosion in storage cost.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for selected model+route and environment across last 1h/6h/24h/7d windows
UI provides explicit io_mode toggle (stream vs block) and stacked decomposition in the percentile chart
Error-rate overlay (5xx + timeouts) renders on same time axis and supports click-through to filtered logs
Clicking a data point opens a list of linked traces (sampled) with highlighted spans for batch-window and KV cache spans
Prometheus/TSDB queries are bounded to avoid per-tenant high-cardinality scans and have CPU/mem estimates documented
SLO/regression alert templates added for top routes and integrated with on-call paging playbook
End-to-end test harness (synthetic traffic) demonstrates that changing io_mode label is reflected in dashboard within 60s
technical_notes: New span tags: io_mode, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, request_shape_cat. Span name convention: servepath.<stage> (e.g., servepath.batch_window, servepath.kv_lookup)
Metric name: servepath.request_duration_ms with labels: model, route, io_mode, tenant, env, sample_rate. Emit histogram buckets for coarse rollups and export quantiles server-side for top-k routes.

Prefer ClickHouse aggregate tables for per-model+route percentiles using approximate_quantileState() to reduce online computation cost. Fall back to per-interval pre-aggregation in metrics ingestion if needed.
Cardinality guard: restrict detailed percentiles to top 2000 route+model combos by QPS. For other combos provide sampled histogram and raw request_count/time histograms only.
Log enrichment: add request_id, model_version, route, io_mode, and error_class to structured logs to enable quick pivoting from dashboard to logs/alerts.
Tracing: ensure sampled traces include KV cache hit span and batch window span; add a tag `trace_hint=servepath-timing-board` when synthetic tests are run so synthetic traces are easy to find.
Latency buckets: 0-10ms, 10-50ms, 50-200ms, 200-1000ms, 1000-5000ms, >5000ms for histograms to cover both short and long tails.
